A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same title, authors, principal results, and appendices A–B. All pages and mathematical content are readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical regret bounds, mathematical examples, and proofs. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including its expanded lower-bound analysis and appendices. It reports no experiments, simulations, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Both versions analyze the same Thompson sampling procedure: sample from the posterior and maximize the sampled linear reward. The corrected likelihood expression in Appendix B.1 repairs the analysis, rather than introducing a different inference procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation tasks. Changes to the theoretical action-set assumptions and covariance coverage belong to T1.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison algorithms experimentally. Discussions of Thompson sampling variants and UCB concern cited theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures are reported in either version.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses. The added sharpness construction in Section 3 is a mathematical argument, assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Changes to concentration arguments are theoretical proof changes.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries or measured findings in either version. Revised regret bounds and mathematical constants are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 6 strengthens the burn-in bound from a truncated eigenvalue sum to a sum over all eigenvalues weighted by min(i−1,T), broadens the action-set assumption, and adds a long-run lower bound for positive-definite Gaussian covariance matrices. Corollary 7 improves the short-horizon scaling from S r d^(-1/2) min(T,d)^2 to S r sqrt(d) min(T,d). Appendix A strengthens Lemma 10, corrects Lemma 12 and summation indices, and adds the second-bound proof in A.2. Section 3 adds a first-term sharpness construction. Further corrections affect Theorem 1's constants, Lemma 5's proof, and Appendix B.1's likelihood and concentration argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same headline contributions: additive separation of prior-dependent burn-in from long-run regret, a generalized elliptical-potential lemma, an unavoidable burn-in lower bound, and extension to strongly log-concave distributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds an explicit interpretation of the two lower-bound regimes and a prior-dependent horizon threshold for long-run near-optimality. The conclusion retains the same limitations concerning log-concavity, Bayesian regret, and a well-specified prior.

D1.justification: Neither version provides experimental implementation details, computational resources, hyperparameters, or code/data access information. The appendix revisions concern mathematical derivations.

R1.justification: The cited works remain the same. Section 4 locally strengthens the paper's positioning by replacing reliance on Rusmevichientong and Tsitsiklis (2010) for a particular scaled-identity prior with its own long-run guarantee for general positive-definite Gaussian covariance.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. v2 makes localized copy edits, changes policy notation, adds explanatory passages and an Impact Statement, and divides Appendix A into two proof subsections. Author-affiliation and citation formatting also change.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts a different template, changing typography, the title and author arrangement, affiliation placement, heading styles, running headers, and page-number footers. Equations and references are reflowed, and the separate Supplementary Materials banner disappears. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the theoretical support for near-optimality: it improves short-horizon lower bounds and supplies a general-covariance long-run bound with a dedicated proof, where v1 relied on a restricted prior result from earlier work. Corrections to Gaussian scaling, eigenvalue indexing, and the Appendix B likelihood also improve central derivations. Local formula inconsistencies remain, including an extra sigma in Section 2.1.3 and an undefined q in Section 3's new construction, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains in theoretical scope and correctness.
